answer: Square-root payout: a cluster of n linked identities earns R times the square root of n, not n times R. A Mesa cluster of 100 fresh accounts collects 10R instead of 100R, a 90% haircut, while a single account still earns R. Bypass: separate funding trees hide links, so the cut binds only where the Sable link graph is accurate; evasion costs one funding source per account. Check rule: anyone recomputes clusters from shared first-hop funders on the public ledger and rejects payouts above R times the square root of n; the Zenith threshold links accounts at two shared funders.
